- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days); cap forecast at 1-2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shifts from neutral to positive mid-horizon, model lags; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d history mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 18d history mean, apply correction based on sentiment direction: + if sentiment positive, - if negative.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; only adjust if sentiment persists for 3+ days.
